items.title: Result Through Another's Power: Why a Bodhisattva Cannot Always Save

items.zh: 與他增上果者，謂亦由受現法果業。猶如如來所住國邑，必無疾疫災橫等起。佛神力故，無量眾生無疾無疫，無有災橫，得安樂住。如佛世尊，如是轉輪聖王及住慈定菩薩亦爾。
items.en: As for giving a result through another's dominant influence: this too depends on one's own karma capable of ripening in this present life. Just as the very city or country a tathāgata dwells in is certain to be free of plague and calamity, so too, through a buddha's own spiritual power, countless beings there remain free of illness, free of plague, free of disaster, and dwell in genuine peace. As with the Blessed Buddha, so too with a wheel-turning monarch, and with a bodhisattva abiding in loving-kindness concentration.

items.zh: 若諸菩薩以大悲心觀察一切貧窮困苦業天所惱眾生，施以飲食財穀庫藏皆令充足，由此因緣，彼諸眾生得安樂住。
items.en: If bodhisattvas, moved by great compassion, observe beings afflicted by poverty and hardship — the working of what might be called their own "karmic providence" — and provide them with food, wealth, grain, and stores until they are genuinely sufficient, then, by reason of this, those beings come to dwell in peace.

items.zh: 如是等類，是他增上所生現法受業應知。

items.title: The Gateway of Harm and Benefit Opens: Eight Ways the Ten Unwholesome Deeds Actually Hurt

items.zh: 損益門者，謂於諸有情，依十不善業道，建立八損害門，何等為八？
items.en: As for the gateway of harm and benefit: with respect to all sentient beings, eight gateways of harm are established based on the ten unwholesome courses of action. What are the eight?

items.title: The Eight Gateways of Harm Named, and a Mother's Love as Proof No One Wants to Die

items.zh: 一、損害眾生，二、損害財物，三、損害妻妾，四、虛偽友證損害，五、損害助伴，六、顯說過失損害，七、引發放逸損害，八、引發怖畏損害。與此相違，依十善業道，建立八利益門應知。
items.en: First, harm to beings; second, harm to property; third, harm to a spouse; fourth, harm through false testimony; fifth, harm to one's companions; sixth, harm through openly exposing another's faults; seventh, harm through inducing heedlessness; eighth, harm through instilling fear. It should be understood that, in the reverse direction, the ten wholesome courses of action establish eight gateways of benefit.

items.title: Karma's Intensification: Six Factors, and a Hierarchy of Severity

items.zh: 業增上云何？謂猛利極重業。當知此業由六種相。一、加行故；二、串習故；三、自性故；四、事故；五、所治一類故；六、所治損害故。
items.en: What is the intensification of karma? It is a forceful and extremely weighty deed. This weight, it should be understood, arises through six factors: through deliberate effort; through habituation; through the deed's own inherent nature; through the significance of its object; through belonging to a class that has never once been counteracted; and through damaging what is to be counteracted.

items.zh: 加行故者，謂如有一，由極猛利貪瞋癡纏，及極猛利無貪、無瞋、無癡加行，發起諸業。串習故者，謂如有一，於長夜中，親近、修習、若多修習不善善業。
自性故者，謂於綺語，麁惡語為大重罪；於麁惡語，離間語為大重罪；於離間語，妄語為大重罪；於欲邪行，不與取為大重罪；於不與取，殺生為大重罪；於貪欲，瞋恚為大重罪；於瞋恚，邪見為大重罪。又於施性，戒性無罪為勝；於戒性，修性無罪為勝。於聞性，思性無罪為勝；如是等。
items.en: As for the deed's own inherent nature: compared to frivolous speech, harsh speech is a graver offence; compared to harsh speech, divisive speech is graver still; compared to divisive speech, false speech is graver yet. Compared to sexual misconduct, theft is graver; compared to theft, killing is graver still. Compared to covetousness, ill will is graver; compared to ill will, wrong view is graver still. Further, compared to the nature of giving, the nature of moral discipline is superior in its freedom from fault; compared to the nature of discipline, the nature of meditative cultivation is superior. Compared to the nature of hearing, the nature of reflection is superior in its freedom from fault; and so on in the same way for cultivation.

items.zh: 事故者，謂如有一，於佛法僧及隨一種尊重處事，為損為益，名重事業。所治一類故者，謂如有一，一向受行諸不善業，乃至壽盡無一時善。所治損害故者，謂如有一，斷所對治諸不善業，令諸善業離欲清淨。

items.title: Karma's Distortion Opens: When Killing the Wrong Target Isn't Quite "Killing" at All

items.zh: 業顛倒云何？此有三種應知。一、作用顛倒，二、執受顛倒。三、憙樂顛倒。作用顛倒者，謂如有一，於餘眾生思欲殺害，誤害餘者。當知此中，雖有殺生，無殺生罪；然有殺生種類、殺生相似同分罪生。
items.en: What is the distortion of karma? There are, it should be understood, three kinds: distortion of function, distortion of grasping, and distortion of delight. Distortion of function is when someone, intending to kill one being, mistakenly kills another instead. It should be understood that although a killing has occurred here, it does not constitute the full offence of killing — yet a related offence, of the same general category and closely resembling killing, does still arise.

items.title: Attacking an Effigy, Two Faces of Moral Confusion, and Taking Wrongdoing as Play

items.zh: 若不誤殺其餘眾生，然於非情加刀杖已，謂我殺生。當知此中，無有殺生，無殺生罪；然有殺生種類、殺生相似同分罪生。如殺生業道，如是不與取等一切業道，隨其所應，作用顛倒應知。
items.en: If, rather than mistakenly killing some other being, one strikes a lifeless object with a blade or club, believing "I have killed" — it should be understood that no killing has genuinely occurred here, and so no offence of killing arises; yet an offence of the same general category, closely resembling killing, still does arise. Just as with the course of killing, so too, correspondingly, with taking what is not given and every other course of action — distortion of function should be understood the same way throughout.

items.zh: 執受顛倒者，謂如有一，起如是見，立如是論，無施無愛，乃至廣說一切邪見。彼作是執：畢竟無有能殺、所殺，若不與取乃至綺語，亦無施與、受齋、修福、受學尸羅；由此因緣，無罪無福。
items.en: Distortion of grasping is when someone holds such a view and establishes such a doctrine: "there is no giving, no receiving" — stated in full detail as every form of wrong view already given. They hold that there is ultimately no one who kills and no one killed, that taking what is not given through frivolous speech likewise involves no giving, no fasting, no accumulated merit, and no undertaking of precepts — and so, by this reasoning, conclude there is neither fault nor merit in anything at all.

items.zh: 又如有一，起如是見，立如是論：若有眾生憎梵、憎天、憎婆羅門。若彼憎惡，唯應殺害。殺彼因緣，唯福無罪。又於彼所起不與取乃至綺語，唯獲福德，無有非福。憙
items.en: Further, others hold such a view and establish such a doctrine: any being who despises Brahmā, the gods, or brahmins deserves nothing but death, and killing such a hateful being produces merit alone, with no fault whatsoever — and that stealing from, or speaking falsely, harshly, divisively, or frivolously towards such a person likewise produces only merit, never any fault at all.

items.zh: 樂顛倒者，謂如有一，不善業道現前行時，如遊戲法，極為憙樂。
items.en: Distortion of delight is when someone, in the very act of committing an unwholesome deed, takes it as though it were mere sport, and finds it a source of genuine, intense delight.

items.title: Karma's Differences Open: Acted, Increased, and Deliberate

items.zh: 業差別云何？謂有作業，有不作業；有增長業，有不增長業；有故思業，有不故思業；
items.en: What are the differences among karma? There is karma that is carried out, and karma that is not; karma that is intensified, and karma that is not; karma that is deliberate, and karma that is not. Karma that is carried out is either the volitional act itself, or the bodily and verbal action that volition, once it has occurred, goes on to produce. Karma that is not carried out is the absence of both. Karma that is intensified comprises everything except ten specific exceptions.

blocks.text: Today's reading answers practical questions about karma. Why can a bodhisattva not simply rescue anyone? What makes one deed weigh more than another? Is killing by mistake the same as killing? It ends by opening a long taxonomy of kinds of karma.

Some results come "through another's influence", as when a bodhisattva relieves beings' poverty. But the treatise adds a qualification: such help "also depends on one's own present-life karma". Master Cháng Bǎi: "Because one has oneself made such karma, one's present body can receive this result through another." Without one's own merit, even a bodhisattva's help cannot land. The text speaks of beings "afflicted by poverty, the 'karma-heaven'". Both teachers explain: people think fortune comes from heaven; in truth it comes from karma, so karma is called "heaven".
This is the doctrinal answer to a familiar question: if Buddhas and bodhisattvas are compassionate and powerful, why do beings still suffer? Help needs a receiver.

The ten unwholesome deeds harm through eight gateways: harm to beings, to property, to a spouse, through false testimony, to one's companions, by exposing others' faults, by inducing heedlessness, and by instilling fear. Venerable Miào Jìng raises a textual question on "false testimony" (友證): it may be a copyist's error, and the Taishō reads 支證.

Six factors make a deed "forceful and extremely weighty": deliberate effort, habituation, the deed's own nature, its object, an unchecked class (doing only harm, with nothing wholesome to offset it), and being counteracted (or not).

By nature, the treatise ranks the ten: among speech, frivolous < harsh < divisive < false; among bodily deeds, sexual misconduct < theft < killing; among mental deeds, covetousness < ill will < **wrong view**. Why is wrong view gravest? Master Cháng Bǎi: "it spreads its influence to many people, life after life." Venerable Miào Jìng: its darkness is the root of all other wrongs. A view shapes every later act.

items: **Distortion of function**: killing the wrong being by mistake. It is "not the full offence, but a similar offence". Venerable Miào Jìng, citing the *Pīxún jì*: one does not go to hell, but may receive a short life as its outflow. Master Cháng Bǎi tells of an assassin who stabbed a dummy under a quilt: the intention was full, but the object was not a being.
**Distortion of grasping**: acting from a wrong view, such as "there is neither fault nor merit", or the belief that killing those who despise the gods brings merit (Day 47).
**Distortion of delight**: taking wrongdoing as play. Venerable Miào Jìng: one who has done wrong should feel dread; to feel happy instead is itself a distortion.

blocks.text: Karma differs in being carried out or not, intensified or not, and deliberate or not. Master Cháng Bǎi: carried-out karma is volition, of three kinds (deliberating, deciding, initiating); only after the third does the body or voice move. Tomorrow's reading explains which karma is "intensified", the kind that will certainly ripen.

quiz.q: The text speaks of beings "afflicted by poverty — the 'karma-heaven.'" How do the teachers explain 業天?
options: people think fortune comes from heaven, but really it comes from karma — so karma is provisionally called "heaven"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "People mostly think good and bad come from heaven; in truth they come from karma — so karma is provisionally called heaven." Venerable Miào Jìng: "What ordinary people call heaven is really karmic force — hence 'karma-heaven.'" The translation renders it "karmic providence."

quiz.q: The text says the result through another's influence "also depends on one's own present-life karma." The reading note says it comes "quite apart from anything the recipient did." What does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: one must oneself have made such karma to receive it — it arises from both sides meeting; without one's own merit, one gets nothing
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Because one has oneself made present-life karma, one's present body can receive this result through another"; "it's not entirely the king, nor the people — both sides meet." The text itself says "this too depends on one's own karma." The reading note says the opposite (logged in the correction list). He also cites the *Mahāyānasaṃgraha*: in five situations, such as a being's own karmic force, even a bodhisattva's giving can't help.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what eight gateways of harm are based on the ten unwholesome courses?
options: harm to beings, property, spouse; false testimony, harm to companions, exposing faults, inducing heedlessness, instilling fear
quiz.why: "First, harm to beings; second, harm to property; third, harm to a spouse; fourth, harm through false testimony; fifth, harm to one's companions; sixth, harm through openly exposing another's faults; seventh, harm through inducing heedlessness; eighth, harm through instilling fear." Venerable Miào Jìng: the first three are bodily, the middle four verbal, the last the three mental. The ten wholesome courses establish eight gateways of benefit.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, through what six factors does karma become forceful and extremely weighty?
options: deliberate effort, habituation, inherent nature, object, an unchecked class, and being counteracted
quiz.why: "First, through deliberate effort; second, through habituation; third, through the deed's own inherent nature; fourth, through the significance of its object; fifth, through belonging to a class that has never once been counteracted; sixth, through being counteracted and thereby diminished." Master Cháng Bǎi: the first four intensify good or bad karma; the fifth, unchecked bad karma; the sixth, good karma that counteracts. (The text's explanations of five of the six are untranslated in the Ru-Yi version.)

quiz.q: By inherent nature, the text ranks the ten unwholesome deeds. Which ranking is correct?
options: speech: frivolous < harsh < divisive < false; body: sexual misconduct < theft < killing; mind: covetousness < ill will < wrong view
quiz.why: "Compared to frivolous speech, harsh speech is a graver offence; compared to harsh speech, divisive speech is graver still; compared to divisive speech, false speech is graver yet. Compared to sexual misconduct, theft is graver; compared to theft, killing is graver still. Compared to covetousness, ill will is graver; compared to ill will, wrong view is graver still." On the good side: giving < discipline < cultivation; hearing < reflection. Venerable Miào Jìng: giving, discipline, cultivation bring merit; hearing, reflection, cultivation bring wisdom.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what are the three distortions of karma?
options: distortion of function, of grasping, of delight
quiz.why: "Distortion of function, distortion of grasping, and distortion of delight." C is fascicle 8's three distortions of affliction. Master Cháng Bǎi: meaning to kill A but killing B is distortion of function.

quiz.q: The text says mistaken killing is "not the full offence, but a similar offence." Per the Pixunji, what result follows, according to the teachers?
options: not hell — only the equal-outflow result of a short life when reborn human
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Per the *Pixunji*, this person doesn't go to hell"; "only, when reborn human, receives the outflow result of a short life." Master Cháng Bǎi: "Yet in a later life one gets a shortened lifespan — so a similar offence of the killing category arises."
